👥 Team ▾
One shared file
No shared file?
Two files in one folder (the older route)

You each keep your OWN file and watch each other’s. Nothing merges by itself — it opens the same review panel, with every conflict defaulting to keeping yours. The trunk above does the same job with one file instead of two, which is why it came later.

You each write your own file. One file both of you write is what makes a sync client leave a second copy called "plan (1).json".
How working as a team works
  1. Put your name on it. Signing as… below. It is stamped on every version you create so the others can see whose work is whose. Nothing verifies it — there is no login and no server.
  2. One person starts the trunk. Start a team trunk… → type a file name and choose a folder everybody syncs (Drive, Dropbox, OneDrive). It creates the file; that file is the shared history. Nothing is uploaded anywhere by this page — the folder is what carries it.
  3. Everyone else joins that same file. Join a team trunk… → pick the file that is already sitting in the synced folder.
  4. Pull before you start, push when you stop. Pull takes anything newer. If you have changed nothing it applies straight through; if you have both moved but not on the same fields, it still applies and tells you who moved. Only a genuine disagreement about the same field opens a review.
  5. Push is refused if you are behind. That is deliberate: pull first, so your work lands on top of theirs instead of beside it.

No server and no account — the file is the whole mechanism, so whatever can reach the file can reach the plan. Chrome or Edge only, and not from a page opened with file://.

Which key goes here? An Anthropic API key — it always starts with sk-ant-.
  1. Go to console.anthropic.com → sign in → API Keys → Create Key.

Not this: your claude.ai login, a Claude Pro/Max subscription, or an OpenAI key (sk-proj-…) — those won't work. API usage is billed separately at console.anthropic.com.

Activity list — 3-point estimates & progress

How estimates, status and inline editing work

Shift-click selects a range · click a Start cell to pin a date.

Enter Optimistic (best case), Most Likely, and Pessimistic (worst case) durations. TE = (O + 4M + P) / 6  •  Variance = ((P − O) / 6)². Edit % Complete inline to track progress.
Status: Critical = zero slack — any delay moves the finish date (shorten it, add people, or re-sequence to fix) • Float n = can slip n days for free • an amber edge = scheduled to have started but still 0% • hover any badge for what to do.
Edit in place: click a task's name, Owner (comma-separate for several people — first = owner, rest attendees, @N for allocation %), O/M/P, Predecessors, Start (📌 pin a start-no-earlier-than date) or Finish (⚑ set a deadline — red when the forecast breaches it) and type. Enter saves, Esc cancels.

Companies

Each company has an id, and that id is what archived activities are filed under — which is how the estimate bank can say how a given partner has historically run against estimate. Two spellings of one firm are two partners, so fix them here rather than living with both.

PERT network diagram (activity-on-node)

          

            
            
            
          

        

        

          

            Detail:
            
            
            
            
            
            
          

          

            📖 How to read this diagram (ES, EF, LS, LF, slack — every term defined)
            

              

                
ESDUREF

                
Activity name
owner • dates

                
LSSLACKLF

              

              
    
                
  • ES — Early Start: the soonest the activity can begin, given its predecessors (counted in working days/weeks from project start).
    • 
                
  • DUR — Expected duration: the PERT weighted average (O + 4M + P) ÷ 6.
    • 
                
  • EF — Early Finish: ES + DUR — the soonest it can end.
    • 
                
  • LS — Late Start: the latest it can begin without delaying the project finish.
    • 
                
  • SLACK (float): LS − ES — how much it can slip for free. 0 = critical path (red): any delay here moves the end date.
    • 
                
  • LF — Late Finish: the latest it can end without delaying the project.
    • 
                
  • Arrows run left→right from predecessor to successor and each one carries its type. FS (finish→start) is the ordinary case and is printed quietly; SS start→start, FF finish→finish, SF start→finish and +n/−n lag or lead change how the dates are calculated, so those chips are boxed and bold. Red arrows trace the critical path. Untick label links if you want the lines bare.
    • 
                
  • Implied links are dependencies a longer chain already gates — delete one and not a single date moves. The Gantt has never drawn them, so the network hides them too and reports the count above the diagram. Tick show implied links to see them as dashed grey arrows, then use Scan & repair on the Tasks tab to remove them for good.
    • 
                
  • Milestones are ◆ diamonds — zero-duration checkpoints (standard activity-on-node notation); they auto-complete when every predecessor reaches 100%. Bottom strip of each task box = % complete; ✓ green = done. Hover any cell for its live values; click any shape to edit.
    • 
              

            

          

          

          
PMI-style nodes: top row ES · DUR · EF, bottom row LS · SLACK · LF. Red = critical path, green = complete. Columns are dependency levels: everything in a column can only start after its predecessors to the left.

            ⏱ Schedule reserves
            
Buffers added AFTER the estimated work, drawn as hatched bars at the end of the Gantt. Contingency = buffer for the known risks in your RAID log — it's inside the date you commit to the client (easiest: click from P80 to size it off the P80 finish — the committed date it produces lands on a whole working day, so it carries slightly more than 80%, and the panel prints the figure it actually carries). Management reserve = extra held by leadership for surprises, never promised. Quote the committed date externally.

RAID log — risks, assumptions, issues, decisions & exclusions

          

            
            
            
          

        

        

          

            

              
              
            

            
One sentence in, a drafted entry out — typed, scored, and linked to
              the activities, stories, criteria or change orders it actually touches. It fills the form below and
              stops there: nothing reaches the log until you press Save.

          

          

            

              

              

            

            

              

              

              
              

                
—

              

              

            

            
Probability and impact are a 1–5
              judgement, and their product is the score the log sorts by — 1 remote / negligible,
              3 even odds / a day or two and some money, 5 near-certain / it moves the date or the
              price. Nothing computes them for you: they are the two numbers you would defend on a call, and only
              their ORDER matters, which is why a rough 3 beats an agonised 3.4.
